note: P-D-2016-42220-7261f9d3, 21 A4 sheets (595x841) of an MCM 2016 problem-D paper on information diffusion, printed 'Page 1 of 20' from PDF page 2. The layout pass measures twenty-eight regions and every one of them is an exhibit: twenty-three figures and five tables, no exclusions. THE NUMBERING IS BROKEN: twenty-three figure drawings carry only twenty-two printed numbers, because 'Figure 5' is printed twice - once for the point-source-flow schematic on page 10 and again for the 'Original network' panel on page 12 - and nothing after it is renumbered. Row identity is therefore page plus region, never the printed number. Citation numbering is broken in the same way and worse: page 12 cites 'three lines in Figure 13' for the Figure 7 sensitivity plot, and page 16 introduces the two capacity plots as 'Figure 11 and 12' when they are Figures 17 and 18. Four of the twenty-three figures are never named by number at all. Every figure is a pasted raster (a world map, an R plot, an Excel panel) captioned below in bold; every table is a vector grid captioned above. Five pairs of side-by-side panels print both captions on one line (Figures 3/4 on page 9, 5/6 and 7/8 on page 12, 10/11 on page 14, 12/13 on page 15). Fourteen of the twenty-three figures are line plots, and they come from three visibly different tools: bare R-style frames, Excel panels with comma decimal tick labels, and one five-bar chart with the values printed on the bars. Defects worth recording: Table 5's Internet row prints 0.12 where the difference is 0.012; Figure 2's caption is clipped left and right by the text column; Figure 19's four horizontal reference lines are unkeyed; Figures 10 and 11 do not share a colour-to-series assignment; Figures 15/16 and 12/13 are each drawn on different y ranges, so neither pair can be read across.
